references.text: Joshua hung the five kings on trees after they were killed, illustrating the same practice of hanging condemned criminals on a tree.
The king of Ai was hung on a tree until evening, in accordance with the law concerning the hanging of executed criminals.
David had the hands and feet of Rechab and Baanah displayed after their execution, a practice related to the public display of executed individuals.
Paul quotes this text and explains that Christ became a curse for us by being hung on a tree, fulfilling the law's curse on anyone who is hung.
Peter refers to Jesus being hung on a tree, using terminology from Deuteronomy to describe the crucifixion.
Peter testifies that Jesus was hung on a tree, a direct reference to the crucifixion expressed with the language of the Mosaic Law.
Paul recounts that they took Jesus down from the tree after completing what had been written about him, an allusion to hanging on a tree.
Peter writes that Christ bore our sins on the tree, using the image of being hung on a tree to describe Jesus' atoning death.
